# Keyed archives

`RSKeyedArchiver` saves the logical state written by `encodeWithCoder()`.
`RSKeyedUnarchiver` uses `robjc_allocate()` to create a current instance
without calling `initialize()`, then passes the saved fields to
`initWithCoder()`. For a singleton class, allocation returns its existing
shared instance. The archive is a plain R list,
so `saveRDS()` and `readRDS()` handle file storage. A repeated reference to the
same RObjC object remains a repeated reference after decoding.

## A registered package class

Classes supplied by `robjc` are registered when the package loads. Their
archives contain a package name and stable class ID, so no resolver is needed.

```{r}
library(robjc)

number <- RSNumber$new(42L)
archive <- RSKeyedArchiver$new()$archive(list(number, number))
record <- archive$records[[1L]]
stopifnot(identical(record$package, "robjc"))
stopifnot(identical(record$class_id, "RSNumber"))

path <- tempfile(fileext = ".rds")
saveRDS(archive, path)
decoder <- RSKeyedUnarchiver$new(readRDS(path))
stopifnot(nrow(decoder$showAllClasses()) == 0L)
classes <- decoder$showAllClasses(remove_default = FALSE)
stopifnot(identical(classes$status, "automatic"))
restored <- decoder$decode()
unlink(path)
stopifnot(identical(restored[[1L]], restored[[2L]]))
stopifnot(identical(restored[[1L]]$nativeValue(), 42L))
```

`showAllClasses()` omits classes found through package registration by default,
so the empty tibble above means no class mapping needs attention. Set
`remove_default = FALSE` to inspect every archived class. The dictionary form,
`dictionaryWithAllClasses()`, always includes every mapping.

## Register a class in another package

Declare the class in your package namespace and register it from `.onLoad()`.
`binding` names the namespace variable holding the generator; it does not have
to match the R6 `classname`. `id` is the permanent name stored in archives.
Keep it stable when you rename the binding or change the class version.

```{r eval=FALSE}
# R/Document.r in package "myrecords"
Document <- robjc::RSObjectClass(
  "Document", version = "1.0",
  public = list(
    title = NULL,
    initialize = function(title) {
      super$initialize()
      self$title <- title
      invisible(self)
    },
    encodeWithCoder = function(coder) {
      coder$encodeObjectForKey(self$title, "title")
    },
    initWithCoder = function(coder) {
      self$title <- coder$decodeObjectForKey("title")
      invisible(self)
    }
  )
)

# R/zzz.R in the same package
.onLoad <- function(libname, pkgname) {
  robjc::robjc_register_class(
    package = pkgname, id = "document", binding = "Document",
    generator = Document
  )
}
```

The defining package should list `robjc` in `Imports`. When decoding, the
unarchiver loads the recorded package if necessary, then reads the registered
binding from its current namespace. Registration holds only the package name,
ID, binding name, and namespace identity; it does not retain the generator.
Use `robjc_register_protocol()` in the same way if protocol generators appear
as values in archives.

Class version is separate from the stable ID. `initWithCoder()` can inspect
`coder$savedClassVersion()` to migrate older field layouts.

## Classes defined in a script

A class outside a package namespace cannot be registered with this API.
`showAllClasses()` marks it as unresolved. Edit the `decoder_class` list column
of the returned tibble and pass it to `setClasses()` before `decode()`.
`showClass(class_key)` displays a single mapping. A resolver callback remains
available for older callers; it receives `class_name`, `version`, and `kind`.

```{r}
Note <- RSObjectClass(
  "GuideNote", version = "1.0",
  public = list(
    title = NULL,
    initialize = function(title) {
      super$initialize()
      self$title <- title
      invisible(self)
    },
    encodeWithCoder = function(coder) {
      coder$encodeObjectForKey(self$title, "title")
    },
    initWithCoder = function(coder) {
      self$title <- coder$decodeObjectForKey("title")
      invisible(self)
    }
  )
)

note_archive <- RSKeyedArchiver$new()$archive(Note$new("draft"))
stopifnot(is.null(note_archive$records[[1L]]$package))
decoder <- RSKeyedUnarchiver$new(note_archive)
classes <- decoder$showAllClasses()
stopifnot(identical(classes$status, "unresolved"))
classes$decoder_class[1L] <- list(Note)
decoder$setClasses(classes)
stopifnot(identical(decoder$showClass(classes$class_key)$status, "manual"))
note <- decoder$decode()
stopifnot(identical(note$title, "draft"))

# The same mapping can be edited as an RSMutableDictionary.
other_decoder <- RSKeyedUnarchiver$new(note_archive)
mapping <- other_decoder$dictionaryWithAllClasses()
stopifnot(identical(
  mapping$objectForKey(RSString$new(classes$class_key)), RSNull$null
))
mapping$setObjectForKey(Note, RSString$new(classes$class_key))
other_decoder$setClasses(mapping)
stopifnot(identical(other_decoder$decode()$title, "draft"))
```

The dictionary uses `RSString` class keys and decoder generators as values.
An unresolved entry has `RSNull$null` as its value. Editing the returned
dictionary does not change the decoder until `setClasses()` is called.

Encode each field with a unique key. Plain R values are left to R's
serialization; ordinary lists are traversed for RObjC references. A class
that stores another RObjC object must encode that field explicitly. The
archive format is currently `robjc-keyed-1` and may evolve during alpha.
